commits.summary: Every example's proof driver records identities, ends the run on a mutant that is not the replay's, and marks a trial
commits.body:
The evidence stream's step 2. examples/tools/beside_route.py holds what the five drivers (examples 286 to 290) did each in their own copy: the pinned JARs, the constructed mutant, the record (accept.record's evidence.json) and the verdict. Each driver keeps its own entry, lemmas, models, observed initializers and verifier arguments. What 289's driver alone did, all five now do: the record of the claim, the bound, each JAR, the adapter, the verifier's binary and the driver; a mutant whose JAR is not the one the newest mutant replay's receipt records ends the run; --max-array-length or --unwind (now on every driver) marks the run a trial.

Finding: 286's, 287's and 288's drivers built their mutant by another recipe than the route's (a fixed --release, no -g or -parameters, every entry recompressed), so their JAR was not the bytes the mutant replay ran, which is why acceptance could not tie their mutant-security answers to the replay. The shared module uses the route's published-mutant recipe; run offline on the pinned JARs it gives each of the five examples exactly the JAR its replay ran (286 48323d21, 287 1d099295, 288 5c72df16, 289 a3a3dbff, 290 4ee35d0b).

It has example 289's three properties: it writes evidence.json with accept.record, a constructed mutant that is not the JAR the mutant replay ran ends the run, and a run at another bound is marked a trial. The second comes from the frozen claim, which, unlike the decision claim, does not restrict the field to ASCII. Job 20261117-130335-example-286-protected-state-tasks-at-the records both tasks at the frozen bound 8 and is expected to exit 1 with those gaps. The example's notes and the brief's Progress say the same.

commits.summary: Models on request of ArrayDeque and HashSet take example 286's DataBinder.bind past its binding result, to the reflection
commits.body:
Every path of DataBinder.bind makes a binding result whose AbstractErrors keeps an ArrayDeque of nested paths and whose AbstractBindingResult a HashSet of suppressed fields; both constructors were JDK gaps under strict gaps. Two models on request now stand for them, as ArrayList's does (lib/models/java/util/lists, models::ON_REQUEST): ArrayDeque as a stack (ArrayDeque(), push with its NullPointerException for null, pop with its NoSuchElementException, peek, size, isEmpty, clear) and HashSet as the keys of the HashMap model (HashSet(), add, contains, size, isEmpty). Both are abstract, as the HashMap model is, so every method they do not keep stays the JDK call it names. AbstractSet() is now an exact JDK call (gaps::exact_jdk_call), as AbstractCollection() and AbstractList() were. Documented in lib/models/README.md and lib/README.md.

Evidence: claims.Deques and claims.Sets (lib/tests/claims.rs, two tool-tier tests) prove each method's JDK answer against its definition written out on every input of a bound with the model, show the class is the JDK's gap when the check does not ask for it and that a method left out (offer, remove) is still the JDK call, and run the same methods on a JVM over 5000 sampled inputs. A mutated model (pop returning the first element; add always true) fails each test. test_costs.py run --changed passed (33 test binaries), validate_example.py 286 passed, examples/tools/test_beside_route.py passed.

Example 286's driver: this line was rebased onto the evidence stream's rkxyyqwn (inbox domain-advances-state-I002), whose shared module examples/tools/beside_route.py now does the three properties; the conflict in proofs/prove.py was resolved into tvxyzwqv by taking the shared module's driver and keeping only each claim's own arguments (ENTRIES: entry, models, observed initializers, unwinding). The decision claim's runs are unchanged from the evidence stream's (no model, the verifier's default unwinding); the protected-state claim's take the three models, unwind 16 and --observed-initializer for PropertyEditorRegistrySupport and CachedIntrospectionResults. Probes at bound 2 (trials, capped at 5 min and 4 GB) of vulnerable-protected-state-mutation now stop at CachedIntrospectionResults.strongClassCache, a ConcurrentHashMap the observation does not hold: the reflection. Inbox item domain-advances-evidence-I006 asks the evidence stream to coordinate observed.rs's format before step 3 extends it. Nothing decided; the frozen claim and the accepted statement are unchanged. The queued job 20261117-130335-example-286-protected-state-tasks-at-the runs the driver as it is now.

commits.summary: A write set, a first effect contract: prove --writes refutes the setter that writes a protected field and proves its honest twin
commits.body: The state stream's steps 4 and 5, the checking side. prove --writes this.displayName (own checker only) states which fields of a method's receiver and object parameters it may write. The check proves the frame with the property: after a normal return every other field of those inputs is unchanged, a primitive by value and a String or object by identity through the new p == \old(p) term. The frame is conjoined to the assertion, so a write outside the set is refuted by the harness and its witness runs on a JVM. Inside the call the engine refuses, by name, a write to anything else that existed before it: a static field, an array, an object no input is (even one a named field holds), or a class initialization, whose objects would look new to the call. This generalizes Engine::keeps through bmc::Options::frame. The cache refuses such a check, since its key does not read the write set.

commits.summary: An effect contract at a call: a setter's checked write set stands in for its calls, and the application-level rename statement is proved through the honest setter and refuted through the adversarial one
commits.body:
A lemma with a writes: line is now an effect contract of a public instance method (prove --lemmas). It is proved first with its frame (the write set of the last commit) and also as reading nothing that was there before the call: no field of the receiver or an object argument, no static field that is not final, no array, no default locale, and no identity comparison of such an object (bmc::Options::closed_frame, which generalizes Engine::reads and Engine::compares as the write set generalized Engine::keeps). What the method writes is then a function of its arguments. In the check, a call on a receiver of exactly the contract's class, with arguments within its bounds, runs a stub of the claim's class (bmc::Effect, the effect intrinsic). A written field takes the parameter the assertion gives it (this.f == p; the expression language now compares a String field with a String parameter by identity), another written primitive takes any value, and nothing else changes. Elsewhere the method runs as written. A written reference field with no parameter, assume:, throws:, array parameters and non-integral results are refused by name.

Verified with lib/tests/fixtures/claims Frames: the honest setter's contract is proved and used (the statement lists it among what the run rests on), and 'an admin stays one under the new name' is proved. The adversarial setter's contract is refuted, so the check that rests on it is refused. Without it, 'a rename makes no account an admin' is refuted by a rename to admin:, and the witness replays. Five use-side countermodels each grant admin on a JVM (Frames.main): a name past the contract's bound, a receiver field a caller set, a static switch, a literal's identity, a subclass hook called through the inherited setter. Each was a false proof with its rule switched off (by mutation: closed_frame off, the exact-class check off, the stub's bounds guard off). New tests: two tool tests in claims.rs and unit tests for the stub, the conjunct split and String identity; test_costs run --changed passes and lint agrees. Inbox item domain-advances-state-I003 is taken in Progress. The brief is not wrong.

commits.summary: Under --gaps assume, a gap whose object is of a class whose model the check runs is refused by name: the models on request no longer read fields no constructor wrote
commits.body:
Inbox domain-advances-state-I004, from the challenge stream (lqyqxwqv): with --model java.util.ArrayDeque or java.util.ArrayList and --gaps assume, the own checker proved that ArrayDeque.clone(), new ArrayDeque(Collection) and new ArrayList(Collection) of one element have size 0, where a JVM gives 1. Assume took the call to make, or to construct, an object with no field written, and the model's size() then read those unwritten fields: a value nobody computed. The engine (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs, the JDK instance call's gap arm) now refuses such a gap under assume when the object it would construct, or the new object it would return, is of a class the checker runs a model of (ClassPath::checker_runs, so the HashMap model the checker always runs is covered too). Under advised, a constructor's contract on such a class is refused as well, since it writes none of the model's fields. Strict is unchanged: the gap is still refused there by name first.

The challenge stream's fixture (lib/tests/fixtures/model-countermodels: README.md, mc/Gapped.java) and its JVM test file are copied unchanged from lqyqxwqv. The README's checker test, a_model_does_not_read_fields_no_constructor_of_it_wrote, is added to lib/tests/model_countermodels.rs. It also requires each refusal to name the call, and it fails with the refusal switched off (a mutation, then restored). test_costs run --changed: 34 binaries pass; estimate, tag and lint agree. No accepted result used the hole, since every example task runs strict. Merging with the challenge line will meet lib/tests/model_countermodels.rs added on both sides: this side is that file plus the one test and its imports.

commits.summary: A write set's frame holds on a declared exceptional exit and is of locations over inputs that may be one object: the challenge stream's three false frames are refuted or proved as JML's assignable states them
commits.body:
Inbox item domain-advances-state-I005 (the challenge stream's countermodels, synvlnls, fc.Framed). Before this commit, prove --writes proved a frame in two cases where a JVM sees the protected field written. In the first, a method writes admin and then throws an exception its throws clause declares: the frame was part of the assertion, which was read only after a normal return. The harness now checks the frame after the expected exception too (harness::generate_property_framed, whose \old reads take their own locals after the assertion's), so rename("b", -1) is refuted with a witness a JVM replays. In the second, one bean is passed as two inputs. The frame is now of locations, as JML's assignable is. Every two inputs of one class may be one object: the check adds the alias choice, and the domain says so. A field that one of them names is framed in the other only where the two differ (this == other || this.admin == \old(this.admin)). So promote --writes other.admin and grant --writes to.admin are proved with that frame, which a JVM keeps, and never with the unaliased one, which it breaks. A write set with a construction plan over two inputs of one class is refused by name. Where a witness throws a declared exception over objects, its expected line now names the frame instead of wrongly saying 'a normal return'.

Tests. lib/tests/fixtures/frame-countermodels (README and fc/Framed.java) and the JVM test in lib/tests/frame_countermodels.rs are copied unchanged from synvlnls. The README's checker-side test a_write_set_is_not_proved_where_a_jvm_sees_a_field_it_does_not_name_written is added, adapted to the location frame: rename must be refuted with a JVM replay, and promote and grant must not prove the unaliased frame. The README's version required those two not to be Verified, which none of the options it lists for aliasing (a location frame, or distinct objects in the domain) would give. A second test proves that what the frame names is allowed on either exit and alias. My own countermodel claims.Frames$Linking#link writes its own name only where other is itself, and claims.rs requires it refuted with a JVM replay. Switching off each fix (by mutation) makes a test fail: the exit frame fails the README test, and the alias pairs fail the Linking case. test_costs run --changed: 35 cargo binaries and 5 of 5 default-tier checks pass; estimate, tag and lint agree.

Merge note: lib/tests/frame_countermodels.rs and the fixture are added on both this line and the challenge line, so a merge conflicts on the test file (take this line's). An effect contract (vwktulky) is proved through the same check, so its stub's writes now rest on a frame of locations that holds on every exit the contract allows. Inbox item domain-advances-state-I006 is noted in Progress: lzpqszyo is not on this line yet. The brief is unchanged outside Progress and still right.

commits.summary: An effect contract stands in for a call only as it was proved: no final static an initializer computed, and object arguments of exactly their classes; the challenge stream's three callers are refuted or refused
commits.body:
The challenge stream's countermodels (qmtxwupn, inbox domain-advances-state-I007) proved three callers through a proved effect contract where a JVM breaks them. The one bean passed twice was already refuted on this line, since the contract is proved with same-class inputs that may alias. The other two are fixed. An effect contract's proof now refuses a read of any static field that is not a compile-time constant, final ones included: an initializer ran before the call in the caller's state, and the proof's ran in the harness's fresh one (Locked.LOCKED = Config.locked). At a call, the stub stands in only where every object argument other than a String is null or of exactly its declared class, like the receiver: a subclass may override what the method calls on it (Rogue.linked sets admin). linkedAdmin is now refuted, with a witness replayed on a JVM. The stub also writes a nested parameter class with a '.', which javac takes.

Verified: the challenge's fixture, README and JVM test are copied unchanged, and its checker-side test an_effect_contract_does_not_prove_a_call_a_jvm_breaks is added and passes. A new claims.Frames case (Mentor#adopt over a nested Honest parameter) is proved through its contract, which is among what it rests on. Each of the three rules, switched off by mutation, fails a test. test_costs run --changed passes (36 binaries, 5 of 5 default tier). Not changed: lemmas may still read a final static an initializer computed (the challenge's item 3, not in this stream's inbox). A merge with the challenge line conflicts on the fixture and test it added: take this line's.

commits.summary: The state line takes the observation binding, and the binding no longer takes a lambda's per-run name for a write: example 286's bind reaches CachedIntrospectionResults again; step 3's account chosen
commits.body:
Example 286's protected-state path (state stream, step 3). The evidence stream's binding of an observed initializer to what it was observed on (lzpqszyo) is copied onto this line unchanged: lib/src/observed.rs, lib/src/observed/ObservedInitializer.java, lib/src/classpath.rs (ClassPath::refused, from mqkqvvmw), lib/tests/observed_countermodels.rs with its fixtures, and lib/README.md's paragraph. It is copied rather than merged because a merge would have this session's sync.py stamp the evidence line's commits made today, as happened once before (rzzuvvwl). On a merge of the two lines these files are identical except ObservedInitializer.java and observed.rs's module doc, changed here as below.

With the binding, 286's probe (fixed-protected-state-mutation at bound 2, a trial) ended before DataBinder.bind. Initializing CachedIntrospectionResults initializes ReflectionUtils, and the binding compares that class's state with its state when initialized alone. It found USER_DECLARED_METHODS to be 'an object of ReflectionUtils$$Lambda/0x000000006604a6e8' in one run and '...$$Lambda/0x000000000e040a90' in the other, and refused the observation as a write to another class. The address is the JVM's name for the lambda's hidden class, and it differs from run to run. The observer now names a hidden class by what it was defined from (R$$Lambda), both for an object it does not hold and for a HashMap key's class. Test: the fixture claims.Hooked initializes claims.Hooks, which holds a lambda, after defining two lambdas of its own. The proof of claims.Hooking#hooked through Hooked's observation is Verified (tests/claims.rs, an_observed_initializer_gives_the_state_a_jvm_left_and_the_result_says_so). With the address kept in the name, the test fails with exactly that refusal. With the fix, the probe stops where it did before the binding: the read of strongClassCache, a ConcurrentHashMap the observation does not hold. Inbox item domain-advances-evidence-I009 tells the evidence stream about the change, since its I008 work edits the same file.

Step 3's account is chosen and recorded in the brief's Progress, from 5.3.19's bytecode. Below CachedIntrospectionResults.forClass the binder runs on reflection and caches. It reaches a ConcurrentHashMap and two of Spring's ConcurrentReferenceHashMaps, java.beans.Introspector, Method objects, some forty default editors and Method.invoke. A held empty ConcurrentHashMap would only move the stop to its get. The next piece is therefore the brief's option 2: a stand-in for AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor.processLocalProperty, checked against the real method on a JVM by sampling, with the resolved setter run as written or through its effect contract.

Verified: test_costs.py run --changed passed (observed_countermodels 4, claims and the other changed tests). The cost inventory test failed only until test_costs.py estimate was run; after it the tiers test and lint pass. The brief's other sections are still accurate.

commits.summary: Under --gaps assume, an object a JDK call is taken to return is of its declared class only where that class is final: HashSet.clone() and Date.clone() are no longer proved to return no HashSet and no Date
commits.body:
The challenge stream's countermodels (lqvlvwsm, wd.Widened; inbox domain-advances-state-I008) showed the engine made the object a JDK call returns under assume of exactly the class its descriptor declares, so a type test on Object clone() said what the JDK's object is not; the earlier refusal (qysmsruu) compared that declared class for equality with a modelled one and missed it. Now the object is of the declared class only where that class is final, and otherwise of one at or below it that the engine does not know (Obj::assumed). A virtual call on it (an override may run), a throw of it, a cast, instanceof or lambda argument cast the declared class does not settle, sameClass, and an effect contract's exact-class test are refused by name; what the declared class settles is still proved. The fixture folder, its README and the JVM test are copied unchanged from lqvlvwsm, and the README's an_assumed_objects_class_is_not_taken_to_be_its_declared_one is added to lib/tests/rule_countermodels.rs. A countermodel of this stream's own, claims.Cloned (tests/claims.rs): Object.clone() of a class whose toString counts, then toString() on the copy, was proved to count nothing, where a JVM counts one. Both tests fail with the flag switched off by mutation.

Inbox domain-advances-state-I009 (286's frozen claim binds one value, so a mutant that checks only the first suppressed value is accepted) is reported in Progress, not obeyed: a claim over two values is a new claim file, the user's decision, and goes into the corrected formalization this stream proposes. Verified: test_costs.py run --changed (38 Rust binaries and the Python suites) passed; the tiers lint agrees.
